The frame transmission time is:

\[
T_t=\frac{512 \times 8}{64000}=0.064\text{ s}=64\text{ ms}
\]

The one-way propagation delay is \(270\text{ ms}\), so the round-trip propagation delay is:

\[
2T_p=540\text{ ms}
\]

For a sliding-window protocol with negligible acknowledgment transmission time, the channel utilization is:

\[
U=\min\left(1,\frac{W}{1+2a}\right)
\]

where

\[
a=\frac{T_p}{T_t}=\frac{270}{64}=4.21875
\]

Thus:

\[
1+2a=1+8.4375=9.4375
\]

Throughput:

\[
\text{Throughput}=U \times 64\text{ kb/s}
\]

For \(W=1\):

\[
U=\frac{1}{9.4375}=0.106
\]

\[
\text{Throughput}=0.106 \times 64 \approx 6.8\text{ kb/s}
\]

For \(W=7\):

\[
U=\frac{7}{9.4375}=0.742
\]

\[
\text{Throughput}=0.742 \times 64 \approx 47.5\text{ kb/s}
\]

For \(W=17\):

\[
\frac{17}{9.4375}>1
\]

So the channel is fully utilized:

\[
\text{Throughput}=64\text{ kb/s}
\]

For \(W=117\):

\[
\text{Throughput}=64\text{ kb/s}
\]

Therefore, the throughputs are approximately:

\[
6.8\text{ kb/s},\ 47.5\text{ kb/s},\ 64\text{ kb/s},\ 64\text{ kb/s}
\]

Answer: C
